evidence: I walked all 2 gate criteria, 38 Functional, 5 Polish and 5 Visual criteria against the frozen reference source. I found no criterion the golden cannot satisfy. Key mappings: (Gates) login 401 on a bad password and recruiter workspace at app.js:197-207; job and candidate creation are SQLite-backed (index.js:202-233) and visible to the Observer via /api/bootstrap. (hro_job_open) blank title, places 0, 51 and 2.5 (client turns 2.5 into NaN, sent as null) and a non-hiring-manager manager_id are refused at index.js:204-207. The team appears in the job selector (board.js:353) and the manager in the facts line (board.js:366). Places show in the Interview heading 'Interview (n of N places)' (board.js:327). (hro_add_candidate / hro_add_email_rules) a new card lands at the bottom of Applied (index.js:229) with source and email in card meta (board.js:251). Invalid email gets 400 and a lower-cased duplicate gets 409, both with field 'candidate_email' (index.js:221-224). The UI shows the error at the email field and never clears the name on failure (board.js:52-57). The same address on another job is allowed because UNIQUE(job_id,candidate_email) is per job. (Moves) checkMove refuses skips with 409, blank reject reasons with 400, rejecting a Hired card with 409 and reopening to a stage other than rejected_from with 409 (index.js:246-256). Cards arrive at the bottom unless before_id is set (index.js:305-307). Up/Down use before_id (board.js:233-241). An Interview re-order adds no entrants, so the limit allows it (index.js:290-295). A full Interview is refused with 409 'limit'. On refusal the client restores its snapshot, shows the reason in role=alert and focuses the card's select (board.js:191-198, 166-171). That satisfies hro_refused_put_back. (Undo) the before-state includes rejected_from and reject_reason, so undoing a reopen restores the reason. Undo is refused if any card's version changed, which covers moves, re-orders and rejects but not notes (notes do not bump version). It is also refused if it would overfill Interview, and it is single-use and latest-only via actions.undone plus the action_id match (index.js:348-373). Restored places follow sorted before.index, which gives Y,W,X,Z,A2 in protocol B(5). Bulk moves are ordered by stage rank and then position (index.js:284-288), giving Y,W,X and A2,V. They run all-or-none inside one IMMEDIATE transaction, and Interview places are counted for the whole set. (Stale) the 409 text includes the card's latest activity detail, e.g. 'F was changed by someone else (Mei Lin moved F from Screen to Applied)' (index.js:241-245). That names the person, as hro_stale_refused requires. (Roles/status) the manager rule is index.js:257-264. It allows Interview/Offer/Hired moves, re-orders, rejects from Interview/Offer and reopens to those stages. It refuses Applied->Screen, Screen->Interview, Interview->Screen, a Screen reject, an Applied re-order and reopening a Screen rejection with 403. Another job's manager gets 403. Observer gets 403 on move, bulk, undo, add, open and note. A candidate gets 403, or 404 for another person's application (mayMove, staffOnly, application()). Anonymous calls get 401 from auth() on every API route, including GET /api/applications/:id and undo. A stale replay gets 409. (Activity) every job opening, add, move, reject (with reason), reopen, re-order and per-card undo is logged inside the same transaction. A refused action throws before any insert. The view filters by job, lists newest first with 'Show more' after 50, and is available to the Observer. (Notes) recruiters can write notes on any card and a manager only on own-job cards (index.js:391-398). Bill gets 403. The Observer reads notes via GET /api/applications/:id. (Live) the SSE 'changed' event fires on every successful write and the client refreshes after 300 ms (app.js:133-157). The proxy pipes streaming responses (bootstrap.js:28-41). Cards are patched in place and focus is restored (board.js:321-341). The detail textarea is never rewritten by syncDetail, which covers hro_live_board and hro_pol_live_board. (Conversations) the newest 30 load oldest first and scroll to the bottom. Earlier pages load 30 at a time with an 'N more' count, and scrollTop is compensated (threads.js:160-175). Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a new line, the body uses white-space:pre-wrap (styles.css:105), and a blank message is refused client-side and server-side. The box is cleared and refocused after a send. Drafts are kept in localStorage per user id, per conversation (app.js:39-43, threads.js:112,124,182). A 401 triggers sessionLost, which prompts sign-in with the email prefilled and keeps drafts (app.js:34,189-195). A network abort gives status 0 with a 'Not sent' message and keeps the text (threads.js:194). Unread counts messages by others after last_read_id. Sending marks the conversation read. Messages arriving while scrolled up add to 'n new messages' without changing scroll or marking read (threads.js:145-158). 'Seen' uses the candidate's read marker for staff messages, and the max read marker of recruiters or the job manager for candidate messages, excluding the observer (index.js:143-150). The Bill read POST fires SSE, so Tomas's page refreshes seen_up_to. Rafael's Board-view page does not mark read because the active check is at threads.js:151-157,212. The seed gives Lena 1 unread (3 messages, read_count 2, third from USR-REC3). Rafael's page reads 120/120 on APP-101. (Candidate) the candidate bootstrap returns only own applications with job_title, team, status label, unread and last_message (index.js:171-176). It has no notes, reason, rejected_from, position or activity, and the SSE event carries no data. Another application's conversation and card detail return 404. Linking happens by candidate email on add (index.js:225). (Restart) seedIfEmpty skips when users exist, and all state, including sessions, reads, notes and activity, is in SQLite at DB_PATH. The Z seed order is Applied Greta, Ade, Marco and Screen Priya, Samuel. Noor's APP-101 note is 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' Both match criteria text. (Visual) the reference has a deliberate stylesheet and the 2026-10-03 board.png shows a coherent board, so it can plausibly score high on the Likert anchors. Runtime: the hash-verified scripted golden run (results/workspace.json) reports 25/25 groups passed with no page errors. The groups include stale with who, bulk and undo order, roles 401/403/404, Interview limit, seen with Bill, unread, paging, drafts, session resume, live arrival in 810 ms and restart. That is supporting evidence only. RISK: no full configured judge run, Oracle grade or measured oracle score exists for these bytes (raw-evidence-index scope says so explicitly). 'The oracle can score high' is therefore source-plausible and script-supported but unmeasured, and that missing measurement cannot be waived. Minor plausibility caveat (P3, not a defect): the candidate view has no list-only state that closes an open conversation. In protocol U 'Move Tomas's page off that conversation (to his applications list)', a judge that leaves the pane open would see Rafael's message marked Seen immediately, because Tomas's open page marks read on arrival. That is correct product behaviour and is avoidable by opening his other application or reloading (candidate openId starts null, threads.js:7), but it is a judge-execution hazard for hro_seen. Counterexample probes: a broken app that is not row 18's subject (e.g. a static seeded board) is excluded by the shared-storage gate. I found no conforming-alternative requirement that the golden itself would miss.
